reason: The 'shoulders' are different things on different parts: the broadened base of a fruit (PO has 'fruit shoulders' as a synonym of fruit proximal end PO_0008002), the top corners of a bamboo culm sheath, moss peristome teeth, an endocarp. With only 19 statements there is no single quality to define.

target: new: coloured marking (a colour pattern value plus the colour of its marks: streaked FLOPO:0991206 or banded PATO_0001946, and red)
reason: Two values joined: a stripe pattern and the colour of the stripes. One class per colour plus pattern would multiply terms. PATO's 'striped' is only a RELATED synonym of banded, which means stripes running across.

target: new: conjunction of two values of one bearer (elliptic PATO_0000947 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Ellipsoid is an EXACT synonym of PATO elliptic. 'Obliquely' adds an uneven, asymmetric shape. Both hold together, so this is not a continuum between two values.
Strophiolate means bearing a strophiole, a seed outgrowth near the hilum (the scar where the seed was attached). PO has the class. Same model as lenticellate (rule C204).
PATO_0002315 means resembling the end of a brush. 'En pinceau' and penicillate (rule C229) map to the same term.

Glands, vittae (oil ducts in the fruit wall) and spikelets that are embedded lie below the surrounding surface. This is the reading used for immersed (rule C329). 'Embedded in X' with a named X belongs to the relation pattern (09).
A plain negation of dilated, which is already the target of 'expanded' (rule C181). The place on the part ('at base', 'at apex') goes to the part-of-the-bearer slot.
PATO discoid has the EXACT synonyms disc-shaped and disk-shaped: a short cylinder that is wider than it is high.

label: porrect
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's projecting straight outward or forward, at about a right angle to the surface or axis that bears it. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0104356 spreading (directed outward and diverging from an axis) and FLOPO:0991207 descending; floras contrast porrect with spreading and descending spines.
reason: A common, well-defined term (276 statements, mostly cactus spines and orchid sepals). No PATO term fits: perpendicular to (PATO_0002434) needs a second part, and protruding (PATO_0001598) says nothing about direction.
Strict stems, branches and inflorescences are upright and straight. Erect is the existing term; virgate FLOPO:0991038 also requires a long, slender, wand-like form.
A spelling variant of spike-like, which was added in the previous review.
'Densely/loosely/evenly foliate' stems and plants bear leaves along their axes, which is leafy. 'Complanate-foliate' adds a leaf arrangement that a separate value can carry.
PATO subulate has needle-like as an EXACT synonym. Acicular maps to the same term (rule C200).
This is a loose count of flowers. 'flowered' is already in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, and 'several' is an inexact number, not a quality.
A spelling variant of hair-like, which maps to filiform (rule C317).
Invisible veins are veins that cannot be clearly seen, which is PATO's definition of inconspicuous. Obscure and indistinct map to the same term (rules C174, C175).

label: lithophytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing on rock or stone rather than in soil or on another plant. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives); kept in FLOPO beside FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and FLOPO:0991111 terrestrial.
reason: A habit term used in parallel with epiphytic and terrestrial, which were added the same way, and often in the same phrase ('lithophytic or epiphytic').
Superposed anther thecae (pollen sacs), ovules and cotyledons lie one directly above another, which matches PATO stacked. 'Superposed on the petals' (opposite) is a relation and goes to pattern 09.
Ribbon-like (French 'rubané') means shaped like a narrow flat band, which is PATO's definition of strap-shaped.

Very short hairs lying flat on the surface. Strigulose is defined as very short, fine, stiff hairs lying close against the surface, and glossaries treat the two as equivalent. The stiffness is the only difference.
PATO arachnose means fine, tangled hairs that look like cobweb. French 'aranéeux' maps to the same term.

A median stamen, sepal, flower or sorus is the middle member of a series or lies on the midline. This is a position of the bearer within its series (kind D of the context patterns), not a quality of the part itself.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1: part of the bearer, apex region) with purple
reason: A purple colour stated of the tip of the part. The region slot (implemented 2026-11-13) carries this as the organ's apex region being purple. The obsolete 'crimson tipped' FLOPO_0980406 shows that colour-plus-tip classes are not wanted.
'Sub-' plus truncated (PATO_0000936, EXACT synonym truncate). The approximate-value pattern covers the 'sub-' prefix, so no new class is needed.
A panicle with cymose side branches is a thyrse: a main axis that keeps growing, with cymes on the side. This matches the definition of FLOPO:0991199.
Gland-like stipules, pistillodes and discs look like glands, which is PATO's definition of glandular. Bearing glands is a different reading and is not meant here.
Asperulous means slightly rough to the touch from minute stiff points. The finer degrees (scaberulous, scabridulous) are already related synonyms of scabrous.

target: lithophytic (new class proposed in this batch; no ID yet)
reason: Epilithic means growing on rock surfaces, the same habit as lithophytic. It is listed as a synonym of that new class instead of being a second class.
Didymous fruits, stigmas and anthers are made of two similar rounded lobes, like twins, which is bilobed.
Veiny means with evident veins, the same as veined and nerved (rules C211, C212).
